english: The porcelain specter does not turn to face you as you approach.
She appears to focus on her work - a series of floating pieces of paper - with her many eyes.
Hi, there. I'm The Cleric. Who are you?
You look scary.
(Poke at her.)
She quickly slaps your hand away.
The quiet in your mind changes its quality. It feels... annoyed.
I am Ettir, she states to you. Yet her mouth does not move.
Telepathic communication.
She is in your head? A parasite...
Not really an introduction, more of a checklist of etiquette.
Speaking with this ethereal creature is unnerving.
I saw you last night, right?
(Stare at the many eyes rotating around her head.)
Yes.
Wow, careful around this one! She's a charmer.
She does not acknowledge your staring. All her eyes are focused on something else.
She is avoiding eye contact in an effort to avoid conversation.
None of them are looking at you? What are the odds?
The celestial appears to focus on her work - a stack of many, many documents - with her many eyes.
There is no acknowledgment of your presence in her many, many eyes.
I am busy.
Busy with what?
(Just look at her documents.)
Notes.
They are a collection of some kind of notes. A diary?
She does seem the type to be deeply in touch with her emotions.
They are detailed notes about the tea shop.
You need help with that?
How dutiful of you.
How dutiful! Dutiful 'n' beautiful. That's an Ettir Promise.
You don't mind me asking some questions, do you?
I do not require assistance, Cleric.
One of her many eyes glares at you for a second, before it rotates past.
Come on... really?
Hm. Maybe she didn't get it.
Good day, Cleric.
Her voice is cold and emotionless.
You might just want to... say what you want.
With all the profitable things in the world you could be doing, you've chosen to hassle a celestial.
Which, if going by the Freestrider's example, will end up being a long and drawn out affair, leading to nothing but a handful of headaches and a couple of genocides.
In short, not very hustlemaxxing of you.
Don't bother with frivolities. Celestials are higher beings, and you must engage them in that manner.
That's... correct, actually.
She is not the type to do small talk. It'd be rude rather than polite.
She is glorious.
If you wish her to speak... you must <shake>engage</shake> with the <shake>elephant</shake> in the <shake>chamber</shake>.
What's it like being an angel?
Can you fly? Or just... float? (Glance at her broken wing.)
(Look around at her messy quarters.) "You, uh... live like this?"
Can you cast spells?
Do you really see out of all those eyes on the halo?
Muster up the courage to ask her about... URTH.
I can't just ask her about Urth. Right?
E-"Okay. Uh. Bye."
No response.
The wing twitches to the side.
Hate to see it. It'd be like if you broke all the fingers on one hand. Or lost your Pouch.
You have the impulse to touch the wing. Maybe you can mend it, make it work again.
You feel a sick fascination with the crippled wing. Dread in your extremities, but you want to touch it.
Do not.
She can talk to your mind but she can also listen to your mind when your mind is the one talking even if you didn't know you were talking with it? That's very interesting.
She is not reading your mind. She is reading your clearly telegraphed intentions.
Really. Don't.
I'm not going to touch it. (Don't touch it.)
What? I'm not doing anything.
It just looks so cool.
(Whistle.)
You hear the goblin groan in the corner.
The celestial does not even look at you. Despite having so many eyes.
Some of her eyes actually turn to stare at you.
Your room at home is much, much worse.
Yeah, but she's an angel. There's probably a higher standard involved.
This mess is a sign that she's an industrious worker. Clearly.
Nothing wrong with a little mess. Just means she's focusing on the right stuff. If you can't get around, that's your fault.
Yes, Cleric. This is my base.
Cool. It's cozy.
It's a bit messy, isn't it?
I thought you'd be a bit more orderly, being an angel and all.
Why?
Her eyes snap to you.
Celestials are supposed to be aligned towards lawfulness.
Her behavior seemed orderly.
Yeah. She seemed like the type to keep things clean.
Uh. Because lawfulness is the alignment of angels?
Just the vibes I got. (Shrug.)
I'm sorry. I didn't mean to offend.
Maybe the divinity of it all had me fooled.
She does not respond.
You've offended her.
She does not seem to care about your comment.
She just keeps working.
Most celestials have innate magical abilities.
She can SEAR you.
Burnt flesh. Burnt SOUL.
All her eyes focus on you for one second.
Your bones quiver.
You feel it. Deep. In your bones.
You clench.
You pause unnecessary bodily functions.
And some necessary ones, like breathing.
Then you focus on the goal.
<shake>Speech</shake>.
R-Tell me about Urth.
The angel's presence causing you to shake.
The body does not hold.
It cannot stand her <shake>overwhelming</shake> aura of divinity.
Could be that she's a hot woman.
Or the divine aura. Either or, really.
(Shake. And, also, shiver.)
Cleric.
Move on.
You must try again later.
This is important.
That depends. Do you think she would respect you for daring to ask such a question?
A man would dare.
A true man.
Besides, discussing Urth should never be off-limits. With anyone.
No. That sounds... horrifying.
Urth's death weighs heavily on his closest servants. This is the type of question that might be wildly offensive to an angel.
But, then again, many of them might want to talk about it, with the expected silence weighing heavily on them. Hard to say.
Yet it is clear in her body language: she does not wish to answer such a question.
Yet... the boldness might also impress her. She appears to be that type of person.
She stops writing.
Get out of here - right now. Run!
Looks like a harmless pause. Just be careful.
Uh oh.
She mimics a sigh.
The faded man-god.
Urth of Norvik.
That's the guy.
So he's your god? You serve him, like I do?
No.
She lifts her hand, pointing towards your chest.
I serve his remnants.
Dzieci Smoków.
Celestial. Meaning something akin to: Children of Dragons.
The term refers to how most humans were slaves to dragons for centuries, before the Arcanists broke those chains.
The dragons do not rule our fates anymore.
Smocko-what?
The city is more than just a remnant.
Interesting.
Hm.
She's impressed.
Her many eyes look at you.
She does not react.
She disagrees.
Not an honorable thing to say. Have you misjudged her?
She leaves no words in your mind.
The celestial turns her head in your direction, just a bit.
She is extremely curious about you.
I uphold my honor through service to the Coinlord.
She should serve you instead.
You should serve me instead.
Sounds like a shitty job.
Good. Stay honorable. Serve the city well.
You should quit. Darrow really sucks.
Hah.
The short laugh echoes in your mind.
A strangely human sound, from this alien creature.
She enjoyed that.
Nice, you made her laugh.
Ah. Great. She's laughing at you.
She turns her head fully towards you. You see through the gap in her skull.
Every eye fastened upon your soul.
You speak like a man with power.
Yet I see but a child.
Her words break your <u>ego</u>.
Your <u>ego</u> is slightly bruised.
Maybe one day.
Maybe.
Hm.
A job.
It's not employment, idiot. As an angel, she's gotta do some kind of service. It's like, their thing.
She does not feel she has any other option.
Honorable.
The angel's many eyes land upon you.
They stay for a while, before she returns to her documents.
She is... amused?
OH yeah! That's working. Keep shitting on her boss!
(Stand tall.)
He sucks ass! Real ass!
Her many eyes now look away.
Okay, that was a bit much maybe.
She turns back to her documents.
I am unsure about many things.
Yet for now, I serve.
For good or ill.
Her stance. It relaxes.
Ever-so-slightly, she settles in your presence.
You've got an in.
She is a fascinating creature. Ask her more.
Gods, she's terrifying.
Yes. She is a horrific and powerful force...
There we go.
Now she will speak with you. For real.
She is still working on detailed notes, her halo spinning slowly around her head.
What do you know about the pale man in the morgue?
What do you think about the goblins?
You have very cool armor.
Do you sit here all day, or what?
R-(Get to know her better.)
E-"Have a good day, Ettir."
No. I am busy, Cleric.
The goblin exhales.
Relief.
Later.
She'll get on board. They always come around.
If you play your cards right, anything's possible.
Disappointed. Highly disappointed.
Good. You are strong enough to carry this team.
Snell actually does a lot. You should appreciate him more.
The goblin? He means well, but he's just a bit of assistance. Barely noticeable.
Men were not meant to carry the world upon their shoulders. Not alone.
Thank you.
She's welcome.
She appreciates your appreciation.
She has practiced the formal way of answering a compliment, because in her culture one does not do such things.
I know. I'm very generous.
No, thank you.
(Stare at her.)
No, Cleric.
What do you do, then?
That's fair. You're not really sitting, just kind of floating.
That is correct.
Score!
When the Coinlord does not require my services, I attend to the archives. From dawn to dusk, normally.
Then I perform a patrol. As is described in my service contract.
A good service to the city.
So... you stay here all day. Then you go out all night.
Sounds boring.
Sounds fun.
Sounds... contentable?
Yes. I work, Cleric.
Her kind do not require sleep.
You are unable to fly, and I am unable to carry you.
Her? Carrying you?
The thought immediately causes you to STIR.
Okay, my guy, RELAX.
No, no. Stay hot on the money. You've got this.
You cast Fly once. It was not worth the investment.
And you got <shake>sick</shake> while doing it...
That is a hobby.
That's one thing to call it.
Contentable? That's the best you could do?
It is a correct word usage.
Yes.
Those feelings are very human.
My service is to the Coinlord.
She is bound by duty. But where does her heart lie?
A truly great woman. Commendable to the utmost level.
It is time.
Become the man you were meant to be.
SPEAK with the ANGEL.
About...
You will falter.
Before the steps of divinity, your manhood crumbles.
As you ask about... uh...
RELIGION.
Get to know her better - by discussing religion.
COWARD.
Yeah. Yeah...
Celestials. A gathering term for creatures born out of and from the Good Planes. There are many such creatures scattered across the Coast.
The only major civilization of Celestials is located in Divinii Torum: The Golden Horde.
Good creatures, usually connected with radiant light and healing things.
This angel sure is one.
Should I even talk to her?
I should keep talking to her.
I shouldn't keep talking to her.
Depends. Will you say what she wants to hear?
She is lonely. But her demeanor does not scream "Please socialize with me."
Her demeanor does scream, Please socialize with me.
She puts down the pen.
Explain.
An assassin is trying to kill me.
Guy's got an iron mask. Like a helmet, but worse.
I really don't have much to tell you. It was some guy with a dagger.
Her halo rotates slightly faster. "Elaborate."
It appears her level of frustration is correlated with the speed of the halo rotation.
You did not notice this previously.
Perhaps nobody with the mental acuity necessary for such an observation is also stupid enough to upset an angel.
Oh. Yeah, that spins when she's pissed. Or excited.
Her halo stops rotating. "Describe it."
She appears interested.
She nods and turns to the desk.
The mask looked real esoteric though.
The angel pulls out a newspaper clipping.
This?
The article is entitled, 'MASKED ROGUE SPELLCASTER STRIKES AGAIN'.
The font is terribly old - Arcane Era old.
Woah. Look!
Beside the article is an illustration. It looks exactly like the iron mask you encountered.
(Nod and look even closer.)
You just have this lying around?
It is from 499 A.E. There were multiple sightings, months apart.
Each an esoteric crime. Teleportation stabbings. Mind control.
Interesting, Snell pipes up in the back.
But no reported sighting since then. And we never caught a culprit.
What about Fireball? Any incidents involving that?
We?
But that's... (Start counting on your hands.)
So this guy's come back to haunt me? Great.
What should I do?
The assassin seemed kind of incompetent?
M-"Thanks for the information. I'll keep it in mind."
No. Otherwise I would have brought it up sooner.
Of course she would have. She's aware of the circumstances surrounding the tea shop as well.
Why? Is she psychic?
Firstly, in a sense, yes. She does talk inside of your mind.
Secondly, no, that does not mean she reads your mind.
Thirdly, she's aware of the tea shop because it exploded. It would be strange if a security professional on Tolstad was unaware.
Oh. That makes sense. Thank you.
Please do better. You green fool.
Wee waa. Wee woo.
I led the investigations unit on Tolstad. At the time.
Angels must live longer than humans. This should be investigated as well.
She sure has been working for these guys for a long time.
A veteran.
Thirty-nine years ago.
Whew. Good thing she told you. You don't have that many fingers.
Perhaps one day...
You'd have to give up pickpocketing, but you could charge good money to show off your forty-fingered hands.
All in all, probably a good thing.
This will be circled back to in the future. Absolutely.
Or it is a copy. Or the mask is magical. Some kind of possession.
Or, yes. The Masked One could have returned.
Call that The Masked Two! Heh.
Kind of like a sequel to the first guy.
Don't say that out loud, but you can enjoy it privately.
Protect yourself.
Wow, thanks. Glad you visited the angel for that advice.
Good advice.
That's not going to end well.
Interesting. Could be an imitation, then. This will be noted.
If you can pursue or potentially apprehend the Masked One, it would be appreciated.
Excellent! You can earn her favor by capturing the assassin.
She's asking something of you? You've actually made an impression.
She wants this assassin bad enough to ask you to do it. Heh. Get to work!
Keep watch.
She closes the book floating before her.
Avoid that creature. There is a darkness there.
Her halo spins erratically for a moment.
I have been told to not interfere.
He is too powerful. You should serve him instead.
Both with the mortician and his helpers.
The pale man's reputation is insane! What the hell is he?
He is surely a powerful wizard in hiding.
Something is certainly off about him.
Oh. But he seems like such a normal guy!
Helpers?
Did he have something to do with the tea shop?
Shouldn't I keep an eye on him, then?
Is he a wizard?
What is he?
Okay. Good info, thanks.
Avoid. Visken.
Mercenaries. Creatures who roam below. Dark spirits.
They are unofficially sanctioned. None opposes their presence, for Visken keeps them in line.
Huh. Another reason not to get in Visken's way.
Do not engage them unless forced.
Not likely.
Visken has been a presence here for almost four decades, to my knowledge. During all this time, he has never caused any issues.
Beyond that, Visken is also in tight cooperation with the Halfway Bridge Tribe. Since they are the main drivers in this investigation, it would be strange if Visken was behind it.
Although if you find any evidence towards his involvement, let me know.
If you wish.
I suggest not engaging.
Don't. You'll just get in trouble.
Don't. You don't have the skills necessary to actually cross that guy. He's something else entirely.
Maybe if you play your cards right, you can get something out of it?
Of course.
At best, he is a weak Arcanist.
At worst, he is a powerful Arcanist.
One who survived the Coast War? That would be... interesting.
A true Arcanist would be fascinating. It is not impossible to imagine.
She opens her book again.
Do not engage. That is my advice.
What information do you require?
...Pretend I'm not here.
He steps even further into the corner of the Guard Tower.
How are they, you know, as a people? Here on Tolstad?
Can I trust their chieftain?
What do goblins... do here? Just in general?
M-"I have some other, non-goblin related questions too."
Weak-willed and powerless as individuals.
A creature that survives through reliance on the group, and on greater creatures.
Ouch.
I agree. An apt description of goblins.
Thanks for sharing.
He gives you a nod along with an expression that says, 'Kiss more ass, while you're at it.'
Her eyes glance at you.
I would describe humans the same way.
You hear a chuckle in the back.
She's calling you weak? Not okay.
She speaks truth.
Yeah, right. Like you're much better.
Fair. We are weak alone. Strong together.
Interesting. (Cross your arms.)
I'm not weak. I'm strong.
No. I am not.
She nods slowly.
A strong man does not need to say it.
That shall be proven in time.
But I do not see it as a negative.
Warmth. Her soul opens.
The voice softens.
Humility and trust are important traits, in all. For all.
Agreed.
Yes. Her words ring true.
Guess she's a softie after all.
Huh. The angel's got some weird views.
Spoken like a true Celestial, bound by selfless ideals.
That is what I think. What else?
Lady Sageleaf is a powerful creature.
Do not trifle with her - or her pawns.
Her many eyes glance at the goblin in the corner.
Her behavior is clean and highly acceptable. However, she does meddle in dark actions when needed.
Hey. I don't disagree. Don't mess with the Old Lady.
She looks at you for a few seconds.
Perform your duties and leave. That is my advice.
She's smart.
Avoiding gangs like that is the only decent way of preservation.
They'll chew you up and spit you out.
If preservation is your only goal, you must raise your sights.
You can do great things in the dark side of the law. If you're careful, of course.
The goblins perform manual labor such as militia duty, construction, various public services, mail delivery, and manning many defensive perimeters in the City Below.
Over the last decade, they have taken up near all such posts on Tolstad.
He points to the angel. "Right on the money." Then he quickly lowers his hand as he remembers he's pointing at a literal angel.
They are also over-represented in crime statistics, and are several times more likely to join and form crime syndicates than the general human or dwarven populace all across the city.
He clicks his tongue. In the far corner.

This appears to be primarily due to segregated housing areas, lack of access to higher paying jobs, and general cultural elements. The goblins are a troubled yet slowly integrating part of Norvik, from what I have observed.
I'd also add that those general cultural elements were fed to us directly from the Norvikian Education Plan.
That is correct. The cultural erasure of goblins was Urth's attempt to avoid this situation. I would argue it has failed.
Sure did.
(Feel awkward.)
It appears to be a highly politicized topic. I apologize if I have made you uncomfortable.
She is correct.
The goblins are troublesome indeed. Lady Sageleaf has clearly cleaned up Tolstad, but most of your other encounters with goblins have been rather unpleasant.
Or, perhaps, the cleaning up has been the result of goblins being more welcomed in Tolstad over the past ten years.
Somewhat more welcomed.
The goblins are scary. They scare you.
You scare the goblins.
It's goblins. They're gonna do what goblins do.
What did Urth expect when he led them into his city?
That they would magically turn into model citizens? Grow twenty inches and turn pale?
Idiotic. One does not mangle folk together like bricks.
The blue one is correct. That is heartwarming to-
Urth should obviously have magically re-educated each of the goblins into mindless servants instead. That would have been future proof - and efficient.
Oh no...
That is not very heartwarming.
Yes. What else?
Imposing.
Ethereal.
Her telepathic voice gets dropped down several octaves.
All the way down your back... your SPINE.
It shivers your <shake>sack</shake>.
This is your chance. Prove yourself.
Show the world: the mountain CAN BE CLIMBED.
Say the right thing.
<shake>Nevermind that, actually</shake>. (Physically recoil.)
Her many eyes stare at you for approximately three and a half seconds.
Then she says, "Okay."
This woman...
She's not the type to appreciate being talked at.
Nor is she one for flattery. Obviously.
She's alien. To you and this place.
This is going to be a bit of a challenge.
But I can figure out what to say, right? I need a follow-up!
You did give her some compliments. Although they might not be appreciated as such.
So now, regrettably there's only one thing left to do.
It's time to bust out the secret move.
Oh no.
Oh yes.
It's time to be genuine.
(Look up at the angel.)
Her eyes stare at you, waiting for whatever words you let out next.
(Clear your throat.)
You hear the telepathic voice in your head.
Cleric.
R-"I think you are very beautiful, and I would like to talk with you more."
(Scream internally.)
Yes, yes. It's painful. Get over it.
She's clearly not the kind to take advantage of your vulnerability.
So just... go for it!
The voice repeats the word halfway before coming to a stop in your mind.
One by one, the rotating eyes begin to look away from you, focusing on the walls, ceiling, and cluttered mess around the guard tower.
Anything but you.
You got her flustered again.
She is genuinely flustered.
Good or bad, you sure have an effect on her.
Now ask what she thinks about you!
Now, whatever you do, do NOT lose your confidence.
You heard me. (Stand tall.)
So... what do you think about me?
You can think about it.
NO! Don't, she'll-
The angel responds with short cold words.
I do not.
They are icy knives in your abdomen.
I have understood you, Cleric.
Her cold expression does not change, but the rotating halo of eyes begins to spin faster and faster.
